title: Idolatry and the Spiritual Realm
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Idolatry is never harmless because false worship opens people to spiritual deception and bondage. Scripture connects idolatry with demonic influence while still holding worshipers responsible before God.
summary: Idolatry is never harmless because false worship opens people to spiritual deception and bondage. Scripture connects idolatry with demonic influence while still holding worshipers responsible before God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ alone reveals the true God and rescues people from idols. In Him, believers are freed to worship the living God rather than created things or deceiving powers.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Idolatry is not merely a mistaken religious preference. Scripture treats false worship as spiritual adultery against God and warns that demons can stand behind idolatrous worship.

An idol may be carved from wood or stone, but the spiritual reality behind idolatry is serious. False worship enslaves, deceives, corrupts desires, and turns people from the living God.

Idolatry can also take modern forms. People may worship power, comfort, success, self, money, control, pleasure, or spiritual experiences. Whatever replaces God becomes a doorway to bondage.

Christ delivers people from idols and brings them to worship the Father in Spirit and truth. The Gospel does not merely remove bad habits; it restores true worship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
This doctrine matters because people often treat idolatry as ancient or harmless. Scripture teaches that false worship is spiritually dangerous and deeply offensive to God.

It also helps those in bondage see that their struggle may involve worship, not just behavior. Freedom comes as Christ replaces idols with the living God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to expose the idols that compete for your trust, love, fear, obedience, or identity. Turn from false worship and bring your desires under Christ. Refuse spiritual practices that mix devotion to God with occult power, superstition, greed, or self-rule.
